Website Service Agreement

AI Rocket and JM Electrical Solutions · Agreement v1 · 21 Oct 2026

This agreement is between AI Rocket, 220 Forest Street, Waltham, MA 02452 ("AI Rocket", "we"), and the business named in the Order Form ("you"). It starts on the date you sign it. The Order Form is part of this agreement. If the two disagree, the Order Form wins.

1. What we build

We build the website and any extras listed in your Order Form (the "Build"). The working preview you saw in your proposal shows the look and features. Before launch we replace the preview's AI-made photos with your own photos, and we add only facts you have confirmed.

2. Launch

We launch within the time stated in your Order Form, counted from the day we receive your deposit. That time depends on you giving us, on time, what section 5 lists. Any wait for a third party you choose or need (such as a domain registrar, Google, or phone carriers approving a texting number) does not count against us.

3. Monthly plan

From launch day you pay the monthly fee in your Order Form. It covers what the Order Form lists for the monthly plan. Work outside that list is quoted first, in writing, and done only once you agree.

4. Payment

  • You pay the deposit when you sign. We start work once it clears.
  • We invoice the rest of the Build fee, and any one-time items in the Order Form, on launch day. Payment is due within 7 days.
  • The monthly fee is charged on the same day each month, starting on launch day.
  • If a payment is more than 15 days late, we may pause the monthly work and take the site offline after giving you 7 days' written notice. We restore it once you are paid up.
  • Third-party fees are yours (for example Stripe card fees on payments your customers make). Fees already included in your price are named in your Order Form.

5. What you give us

  • Your own photos, prices, hours and business facts, and quick answers to our questions.
  • Access to your Google Business Profile, or an invitation as a manager.
  • You confirm that you own, or have the right to use, everything you give us, and that your prices and claims are accurate.

6. Term and cancelling

The monthly plan has a 3-month minimum from launch day. After that it runs month to month. Either side may end it with 30 days' written notice; email or text counts. Either side may end this agreement at once if the other seriously breaks it and does not fix it within 15 days of written notice.

7. What you keep when it ends

Once you have paid the Build fee in full, you own your site's content: your text, photos, prices and logo. When the plan ends we hand over the site files and move your domain to you. The deposit is not refunded once work has started. Monthly fees already paid are not refunded.

8. Our tools

We keep ownership of the general tools, templates and code we use for all clients. You get a permanent licence to use them as part of your site. We may show your site in our portfolio unless you tell us in writing not to.

9. No promises about results

We do the work listed in good faith. We cannot promise any search ranking, number of visitors, bookings or sales, because Google and your customers decide those. Third-party services (hosting, Google, Stripe, phone carriers) can change or go down, and we are not responsible for their outages.

10. Limit of liability

Neither side is liable for lost profits or indirect losses. Our total liability under this agreement is limited to the fees you paid us in the 3 months before the claim. This does not limit liability for fraud or wilful misconduct.

11. Privacy

We use customer details collected by your site (such as bookings) only to run your site, and we never sell them. You are responsible for any privacy notice your business needs, and we will add one to your site if you ask.

12. Electronic signature and notices

You agree to sign electronically. Typing your name and ticking "I agree" on the proposal page is your signature, and it has the same effect as signing on paper. Written notice may be given by email or text to the contacts in the Order Form.

13. General

Massachusetts law governs this agreement. Any dispute goes to the courts of Middlesex County, Massachusetts. This agreement and the Order Form are the whole deal between us; changes must be in writing and agreed by both sides. If a part is found unenforceable, the rest still stands.
